The '''JT-12 jetpack''' was a personal [[Jetpack/Legends|jetpack]] manufactured by [[Merr-Sonn Munitions, Inc./Legends|Merr-Sonn Munitions, Inc.]] prior to the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]].

The JT-12 was a compact jetpack featuring an [[MM9 mini concussion rocket launcher/Legends|MM9]] [[Missile launcher/Legends|missile launcher]]. This model was similar to the more heavily-armored [[Z-6 jetpack/Legends|Mitrinomon Z-6]] jetpack. Both models were favored by the [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Jango Fett/Legends|Jango Fett]].

==History==
[[File:Jetpack_-_SWGTCG.jpg|thumb|left|200px|A close-up on a JT-12 jetpack used during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]]]
While Fett was hunting down [[Meeko Ghintee]], he lost his JT-12 when an arena insectoid Borhek hit him. Fett found his JT-12 on the [[Outland Transit Station]], using it to track down his bounty, Meeko Ghintee, through the twisting streets of the station's commercial sector. Fett continued to alternate between his JT-12 and Z-6 models, until the latter was destroyed during a battle with [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] on [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]]. Fett equipped his JT-12 during the flight to [[Geonosis/Legends|Geonosis]], later using it to launch himself into the [[Petranaki arena]] to face [[Mace Windu/Legends|Mace Windu]] in single combat. However, Fett was charged by a disgruntled [[Reek/Legends|reek]], and his jetpack suffered damage. Mace Windu sensed that he could kill Jango because he was now weakened and injured. Fett, off-balance and weak from the reek attack, noticed Windu charge at him. Jango tried to fire his jetpack, but the device failed to launch. With an arcing swing of his [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]], Windu decapitated the injured bounty hunter, severing the top of the warhead [[Missile/Legends|missile]] in the process.

A modified version would be used extensively by [[Clone jet trooper/Legends|clone jet troopers]] and members of the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] [[Death Watch/Legends|Death Watch]], who replaced the MM9 missile with the larger Z-6 antivehicle homing missile.

Similar to the Z-6, the fuel tank held enough fuel for one minute of continuous operation (20 three-second blasts). Each three-second blast moved the wearer up to 100 meters horizontally or 70 meters vertically. A user of standard height and weight could reach a top speed of 145 kilometers per hour with a maximum range of two kilometers. Directional thrusters featured gyro-stabilizers to apply counterthrust for maneuvering and landing.
